report:
**Conclusion:** The health claim is **true**. In pregnant women with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection and high maternal viral load, initiating tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) therapy in the third trimester significantly reduces the risk of mother-to-child transmission.

**Evidence Summary:**
* **Clinical Efficacy:** Pregnant women with high maternal viral loads (typically defined as HBV DNA $\ge 200,000\text{ IU/mL}$ or $\ge 5.3\log_{10}\text{ IU/mL}$) face a notable risk of transmitting HBV to their infants, even when standard infant immunoprophylaxis (hepatitis B vaccine and immune globulin) is given at birth. Randomized trials show that starting daily tenofovir at 28 to 32 weeks of gestation substantially suppresses maternal viral load prior to delivery, lowering transmission rates compared to standard care alone.
* **Global Guidelines:** The World Health Organization (WHO) and global hepatology organizations recommend tenofovir prophylaxis starting from 28 weeks of pregnancy for HBV-infected pregnant women with high viral levels or HBeAg positivity to prevent perinatal transmission.
* **Safety:** Clinical evidence confirms that third-trimester tenofovir treatment is well tolerated by pregnant women and does not increase the risk of adverse birth outcomes or infant safety issues.

**Sources Cited:**
* NYU Langone Health: https://nyulangone.org/news/antiviral-treatment-during-pregnancy-reduces-mother-child-transmission-hepatitis-b
* PubMed Central: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5719592/
* World Health Organization: https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/978-92-4-000270-8
* The Lancet Infectious Diseases: https://www.thelancet.com/journals/laninf/article/PIIS1473-3099(20)30586-7/abstract
